best_for: Windows 10 and 11 users who want moving wallpapers, from videos to web pages and shaders, without a paid app or a hit to game performance.
description:
Lively Wallpaper is an app for animated desktop backgrounds, made by the developer rocksdanister and shared on GitHub. It is a native Windows app built with Microsoft's WinUI 3, and volunteers translate it into other languages.

To set a wallpaper, drag a video file or a web page onto Lively and drop it. Videos play through mpv or VLC with hardware acceleration, and you can add video filters. You can also control Lively from the command line, or from Python or AutoHotKey scripts. If you build your own wallpapers, the Lively API can feed them hardware readings, an audio graph and details of the song that is playing.

points.title: More than video loops
points.text: Lively can use videos, GIFs, web pages, Shadertoy shaders and even Unity or Godot games as your desktop background. Web pages and games stay interactive.

points.title: Steps aside for games
points.text: Playback pauses when a full-screen app or game is running, bringing CPU and GPU use near zero. It can also pause on battery power or during a remote desktop session, and you can set rules per app.

points.title: Several monitors
points.text: Lively has per-screen and span layouts for several monitors, and version 2.2.1 lets you choose which display's wallpaper plays sound. It can also run as a screensaver.

points.title: Windows only, and free
points.text: There is no macOS or Linux version. Lively is free and open source under the GPL v3, with no paid tier.

points.title: Installer or Store
points.text: The installer needs Windows 10 version 1903 or later and installs machine-wide. The Microsoft Store version runs on 1809 and later, but it cannot switch to beta builds.

points.title: Versions kept here
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 25 versions, so you can step back if a new release misbehaves with your setup.
